bullets.title: Fed hiked 25bp; market prices 84%+ chance of another hike; hawkish Warsh signals higher-for-longer
bullets.body: The Fed raised rates 25bp unanimously to 3.75-4.0%, with Chair Warsh signaling financial conditions are not yet restrictive and flagging persistent inflation. The dot plot shows 16 of 18 officials project at least one more hike in 2026; markets subsequently priced 84-88% odds of a follow-on hike, with Goldman and BofA each penciling in an October move. Hedgeye sees 2yr/10yr yields targeting 4.85%/5.12% cycle highs, while 22V notes the mild-tightening backdrop favors AI-services names over cyclicals.

bullets.title: US 10-year yield breached 5% for first time since 2007; global rate regime shifting hawkish
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury crossed 5% intraday during the week before retreating slightly to ~4.98-5.01%. French 10-year yields hit 4.56% (highest since 2008), the French-German OAT-Bund spread widened to 100bp (widest since 2012), and JPM raised its YE26 10-year target to 5.05%. The BOJ also hiked 25bp to 1.25% (31-year high), though dovish dissents caused the yen to weaken. Western European central banks (BoE, ECB, Riksbank, Norges Bank) are broadly tilting hawkish, with ECB expected to hike again in December and JPM projecting a March 2027 follow-on.

bullets.title: Anthropic AI-pacing essay triggers largest-ever single-day Software-over-Semis rotation (+12%+)
bullets.body: Dario Amodei's weekend essay calling for slower frontier model development—backed by Altman and Musk—sparked the biggest one-day Software vs. Semis divergence on record: SOX fell ~5-6% while IGV gained ~5%, a ~12% spread (2.4-sigma move). Analysts broadly concluded a genuine slowdown is unlikely given US-China competitive dynamics, and both Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan publicly dismissed the concerns, with Tan reaffirming AVGO's $115B FY27 AI semiconductor revenue target. Trump called Huang on stage at the All-In Summit to oppose AI slowdown rhetoric. The sell-off was widely characterized as a buying opportunity in semi hardware names.

bullets.title: Saudi East-West pipeline offline; Strait of Hormuz disrupted; Brent ~$100-106; diesel at record $6.45/gallon
bullets.body: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was struck by Houthi drones and expected offline 3-5 weeks, forcing Saudi crude to route through Hormuz. Aramco suspended next-month crude allocations to European refiners. Vessel traffic through Bab el-Mandeb fell to well below a third of 2024 averages, and Hormuz commodity vessel crossings dropped to 4/day vs. a 10-day average of 16. US diesel hit a fresh all-time high of $6.45/gallon (AAA), WTI consolidated near $96-106 depending on geopolitical headlines, and Dated Brent ended the week around $130/bbl. Airlines including United and Southwest began cutting capacity on fuel cost pressures.

bullets.title: Geopolitics: Iran sanctions signed; Trump-Xi summit Sept 24 key; IRGC fires cruise missiles near Hormuz
bullets.body: Trump signed the Russia sanctions bill. IRGC-Navy fired at least 5 cruise missiles at ships in or near the Strait of Hormuz, and UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unknown projectile. US Treasury Secretary is scheduled to discuss AI and rare earths with China's Vice Premier; the Trump-Xi state dinner drew attendance from Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Apple's Tim Cook, OpenAI's Altman, JPMorgan's Dimon, and Citi's Fraser—signaling high-level tech diplomacy ahead of the Sept 24 summit. Rare earth deal expiration (Nov 10) and tech export controls are top agenda items.

bullets.title: Semiconductor capex cycle intact; Jensen says chip sales will double YoY; CoWoS demand-supply gap narrows to 10%
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated he expects chip shipments to roughly double next year, driven by broad AI adoption across industries. JPM's semiconductor team raised TSMC CoWoS capacity estimates 4-6% for 2027-28 (200K/225K wfpm by year-end 2027/28) and noted the demand-supply gap has narrowed to ~10%, with leading-edge wafers and substrates now the bigger bottlenecks. AMD plans a 10% price hike in Q4 on rising TSMC costs; Corning is raising display glass prices 15% from Q4. Semiconductor customer inventory reached 58 days (+4 q/q), flashing a yellow flag but datacenter commentary remains robust.

bullets.title: Memory price supercycle accelerating; INTC CEO says prices up 5-7x; SK Hynix/INTC US fab deal in talks
bullets.body: Intel CEO stated memory prices have surged 5-7x, with memory now comprising ~75% of cost for some lower-end phones and laptops; SK Hynix flagged 2027 as potentially the worst supply year. Micron has $100B in take-or-pay contracts. RBC channel checks project 80-100% HBM ASP hikes for 2027. Separately, Reuters reported SK Hynix is in early talks with Intel about leasing capacity at Intel's Ohio facility or forming a JV to manufacture memory chips in the US—the first such arrangement—with Citi flagging it could reduce US market lead time by 4-5 years.

bullets.title: Meta Muse hits #1 on Apple App Store; Muse subscription monetization launched
bullets.body: Meta's new AI agent Muse reached #1 on the US Apple App Store, surpassing ChatGPT, after accumulating ~900K downloads in its first week. Morgan Stanley estimates 100M Muse users could add ~1% to 2028 EPS, with 15%+ upside if transaction monetization materializes. Meta simultaneously launched a tiered Meta One subscription service starting at $2.99/month. Citi opened a 90-day upside catalyst watch ahead of Meta Connect (Sept 23-24) where a new foundation model (codename 'Watermelon') and next-gen glasses are expected.

bullets.title: AI capex ecosystem undisturbed: hyperscaler IG issuance forecast $420B in 2027; compute prices rising
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs forecasts $420B of global hyperscaler gross debt issuance in 2027, up ~68% from 2026, as capex revisions continue upward. Nebius and CoreWeave both raised GPU rental prices 17-21%, with short-term power contracts running ~$40M/MW. Crusoe raised $3.9B Series F at $30.9B valuation for AI infrastructure. AI-related debt issuance tracked $578B YTD. Anthropic is targeting 10GW of compute capacity by end-2027 (doubling from current). Jefferies semis bus tour participants universally confirmed demand far outpaces supply.

bullets.title: US macro data broadly missed: Industrial Production flat, manufacturing -0.3%, LEI -0.1%; Empire slipped
bullets.body: August Industrial Production came in flat vs. +0.3% consensus, with manufacturing down 0.3% (vehicle production down for second consecutive month). The Conference Board Leading Economic Index fell 0.1% vs. +0.1% expected. The September Empire State Manufacturing Index fell 13 points to 7.6 (ISM-equivalent 53.7), with prices paid rising to their highest since 2022. August retail sales beat strongly at +1.2% headline (+1.4% control group), driven by e-commerce and electronics. 3Q real GDP estimates were revised up by MS to 2.4% on retail strength.

bullets.title: Labor market accelerating: claims sub-200K for first time since mid-July; wage inflation risks rising
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 196K, the first sub-200K print since mid-July and near multi-decade lows. Continuing claims dropped to 1.73M, lowest since early 2024 and down ~10% YoY. Hedgeye's Macro Show flagged ADP data showing re-firming in hiring over the past 4 weeks, with Indeed Job Postings set to turn positive for the first time post-pandemic. Regional Fed surveys on wages are rising and small business hiring plans are near highs, with cyclical wage growth accelerating—signaling mounting inflationary pressure that could pull forward additional Fed hikes.

bullets.title: BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.25% (31-yr high); dovish dissents weaken yen; rate-check intervention signaled
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised its overnight call rate 25bp to 1.25% in a 7-2 decision. Two dissenting votes and Governor Ueda's cautious language on the pace of further hikes sent the yen sharply lower, with USD/JPY breaking above 157 for the first time since early September. The BOJ subsequently conducted FX rate checks per Nikkei, viewed by markets as an attempt to spook yen shorts. Citi revised its BOJ rate forecast to hikes in December 2026, March, and July 2027. JGB yields fell modestly post-meeting as energy-inflation concerns eased.

bullets.title: European sovereign stress: France 10Y at 2008 high; OAT-Bund spread at 100bp (2012 high)
bullets.body: The French 10-year bond yield rose to 4.56%, the highest since 2008, as the French-German spread widened to 100bp—its widest since the Eurozone crisis of 2012. EU Economic Commissioner Dombrovskis warned rising bond yields will affect all of Europe and called for stronger fiscal policies. Germany's August PPI came in at 4.6% YoY, well above the 3.9% consensus. JPM now forecasts the ECB to deliver a fourth hike in March 2027, bringing the deposit rate to 3%.

bullets.title: Goldman CTAs positioned as sellers in all scenarios; panic index jumps; positioning cleaner post-deleveraging
bullets.body: Goldman's equity flows team warned that CTAs are positioned as sellers in all market scenarios next week. The panic index jumped alongside slumping sentiment, with Goldman's macro traders separately characterizing positioning as cleaner after a deleveraging event. US equity ETF flows hit -2 standard deviations on 1-week and 4-week basis—the most negative since late Q1 2026. Hedge fund net leverage is at the 18th percentile of the past year, with the L/S ratio at 2.2 as of Friday after aggressive re-grossing in semis and memory names post-FOMC.

bullets.title: Global financial conditions tightening; CCC credit spreads above 900bp; BoE signals November hike
bullets.body: Hedgeye noted CCC credit spreads widened above 900bp, with borrowing costs for weaker credits approaching ~15%. Private credit default rates hit a record 6.3% per Fitch. The BoE held at 3.75% but signaled intent to hike in November, with JPM now expecting November and February 2027 hikes; UK CPI accelerated to 3.1%. Globally, JPM's DM strategy team forecasts ~100bp of cumulative DM rate hikes through mid-2027, with six of nine DM central banks expected to hike by end-2026.

bullets.title: $7T quad-witching options expiry on Sept 18 is 2nd-largest on record; SPY near $3.7B put wall at 760
bullets.body: Friday's quad-witching event involved ~$7 trillion in notional open interest, the second-largest expiry ever recorded. Separately, SPY returned to a $3.7B put wall at the 760 strike ahead of expiry. Goldman flagged $19.5B in global CTA selling risk if markets remained weak into the event, and Citi estimated negative-gamma regime implications if SPX breaks 7,600. SPX immediate-term risk range was characterized as 7,513-7,727 by Hedgeye entering the week.

bullets.title: California governor signs AI kill-switch order; House votes on Ratepayer Protection Act; chip export control pressure
bullets.body: California Governor Newsom signed an executive order directing the development of an AI 'kill switch' capability for advanced AI systems. The House is voting on the Ratepayer Protection Act, which would force data centers to absorb infrastructure costs rather than passing them to ratepayers; 65% of voters oppose unhindered data center expansion. House China Panel Chair Moolenaar urged Trump to tighten AI chip export controls to China. A Texas governor's race tightening toward a candidate pushing data center moratoriums was flagged as a longer-term regulatory risk.

bullets.title: Anthropic expected to IPO in 2026 at ~$2T valuation; NVDA in talks for $10B anchor investment
bullets.body: Axios reported Anthropic is still expected to list in 2026 on Nasdaq with Morgan Stanley and Goldman as lead underwriters, targeting a ~$2T valuation and potential $100B total raise. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest up to $10B as anchor investor. Anthropic disclosed positive adjusted operating income for the second consecutive quarter with >80% gross margins. OpenAI separately confirmed its IPO will not occur in 2026, delaying to at least 2027. The Anthropic IPO is widely viewed by sell-side analysts as the single most important catalyst to reignite the broader AI trade.

bullets.title: US consumer resilient but K-shaped; 401(k) balances up 10.5% in Q2; real wages improving at low end
bullets.body: Average 401(k) balances rose 10.5% in Q2—the biggest quarterly gain since 2020. Inflation-adjusted median household income reached an all-time high. August retail sales beat strongly (+1.2% headline, +1.4% control). However, 85% of Americans say their personal financial situation is getting worse or staying the same per FOX survey. Diesel at $6.45/gallon and gasoline at $4.43/gallon (record for this point in September) are squeezing lower-income consumers and airlines. AAII bull-bear sentiment spread hit its lowest since May 2025, remaining below its historical average for the 9th consecutive week.

bullets.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman; Howard Buffett assumes role effective immediately
bullets.body: Warren Buffett stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway ($1T conglomerate) effective immediately, moving to chairman emeritus. His son Howard G. Buffett assumed the chairman role. Greg Abel was reaffirmed as successor/leader of the company. The transition was characterized as orderly and consistent with Buffett's long-stated succession plan.
